principle_correct.critique: The answer names the right principle. Entanglement decays as the state grows, because each added qubit adds a gate, a qubit that can lose its state, and a readout that can be wrong. It states this correctly. It also says that one error on any qubit breaks the all-agree pattern. One small overclaim is present. The answer says the even split of all-0 and all-1 is what a GHZ state should give. That is true, but a non-entangled mix of all-0 and all-1 would also give that split. Agreement alone does not prove entanglement. This does not make the main physics wrong.
